episodes.173791: A strong surface low developed and led to strong winds, record warmth, severe thunderstorms, and grass fires. Peak observed winds were between 60 - 70 mph. A few hail reports were also received.
episodes.174418: A brief, weak tornado occurred in Cherryville with minor damage.
episodes.174504: Very strong deep-layer shear developed as a result of an increase in the low-level jet and turning mid-level winds ahead of the approaching strong upper-level trough. A strong push of mid-level instability created up to 1000 J/kg MUCAPE, despite an environment with a strong sub-cloud dry layer.  Storms moved rapidly northeast, with a cluster of hail producing storms in east central South Dakota. A second round of wind-producing storms erupted on the nose of the low-level jet across far northeast Nebraska, and translated quickly through southeast South Dakota into northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota. |Strong synoptic winds were observed well to the north of the storms toward the southeast side of the Sioux Falls metro area with some reports of wind damage.
episodes.174505: Very strong deep-layer shear developed as a result of an increase in the low-level jet and turning mid-level winds ahead of the approaching strong upper-level trough. A strong push of mid-level instability created up to 1000 J/kg MUCAPE, despite an environment with a strong sub-cloud dry layer.  A cluster of wind-producing storms developed and moved rapidly northeast from Nebraska into South Dakota on the nose of the low-level jet.
episodes.174781: The wet trend continued by the end of the month as another TUTT approaches the area. At first, this mid to upper level feature combined with moisture being pulling from the deep tropics into the region. Later in the period, a tropical wave was added to the mixture, further increasing moisture content and instability. A Flash Flood Watch was issued due to the excessive rainfall expected.

events.narrative: A brief, weak tornado occurred on Saturday evening northeast of Cherryville, OR. Video confirmation was obtained, as well as a storm damage survey.  It did cause damage to trees, powerlines, a vehicle, one residence, and small outbuildings. Estimated wind speeds of 75 to 85 mph which rates this tornado as EF-0.
Minor mudslides and rocks on the road on Highway 18 near Panorama Point. Rain of 0.43 inch reported in four hours.
Personal weather station measured a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
Albion AWOS measured a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
Emergency managers reported that a section of road PR-140 over southwestern Utuado was blocked due to a mudslide.
Emergency manager reported a destroyed grain bin.
Public reported multiple vehicles damaged by 1.25-inch hail.
Personal weather station measured a peak wind gust of 72 mph.
Public reported a car damaged due to downed tree limb.
Several moderate-sized branches were downed by thunderstorm wind gusts.
